messages.content: Plan me a half-day heritage walk

Here’s a quick, fun half‑day heritage walk that hits three must‑see spots:

• **Start at Jumeirah Mosque** (30 min – 1 hr)  
  – Dress modestly; women need a headscarf.  
  – Join a short guided tour (outside prayer times) with a local Muslim guide.  
  – Peek into the “Once Upon a Time” museum to get a quick history of Dubai.  
  – Grab a bite of Emirati food in the on‑site dining area before the tour ends.

• **Walk (or hop on a quick bus) to Dubai Heritage Village** (1 hr)  
  – Open Sunday‑Thursday 8:00‑22:00; Friday‑Saturday 3:00‑22:00, so you’ll be fine in the morning.  
  – Explore traditional wind‑tower houses, crafts, and live demos of old‑school Emirati life.  
  – The site is run by Dubai Culture & Arts Authority, so everything feels authentic.

• **End at Al Fahidi Fort (Dubai Museum)** (1 hr 30 min)  
  – Wander through three vivid dioramas:  
    – Desert life – date farm, camel, Bedouin tent packed with jewelry and daily‑use items.  
    – Sea life – building a dhow, local marine species, and seafaring gear.  
    – Archaeology – a snapshot of ancient digs.  
  – The walls even share Bedouins’ star‑navigation tricks.

**Timing tip:**  
Start around 9 am, finish by 1 pm. You’ll get a solid heritage dose without rushing, and still have the afternoon free for more Dubai fun!

ession. Visitors must follow standard mosque dress standards: adults must wear modest clothing and women must wear headscarves. Tours are led by individual Muslim guides of varying national and ethnic backgrounds, and take place outside of times of prayer.
The complex also features multiple areas largely intended for tourists: the on-site Once Upon a Time museum covering the history of Dubai; the majlis, which includes a gift shop; and a dining area where Emirati food is served prior to tours.
